name: Hatting
kurzbeschreibung: Charming village in the Unterinntal with an idyllic setting between the Inn river and the foothills of the Tuxer Alpen.
beschreibung:
Overview

Hatting is located at an altitude of 616 metres in the Tyrolean Inn Valley within the district of Innsbruck-Land, about 18 kilometres west of the provincial capital Innsbruck and roughly ten kilometres east of Telfs. The municipality encompasses just over five square kilometres and is home to around 1,500 residents. Spreading across a fertile alluvial fan south of the River Inn, the village snuggles against the scenic foothills of the Stubai Alps. Hatting is distinguished by its quiet rural residential charm, free from industrial noise. Thanks to its prime location in the valley, the village provides a perfect base for peaceful riverside cycling as well as alpine hikes and mountain biking into the surrounding peaks.

History

Settlement in this area dates back to the early Bavarian land-taking period, as evidenced by the traditional -ing suffix indicating the settlement of the clan of Hatto. Hatting was first mentioned in historical documents in the 11th century. For centuries, the village shared a close administrative bond with neighbouring Inzing; between 1974 and 1993, the two municipalities were temporarily merged before Hatting successfully regained its political independence in 1993. The architectural landmark of the village is the Parish Church of St. Giles (St. Ägidius). Originating in the late-Gothic period with its striking pointed steeple, the church was remodeled in the Baroque style during the 18th century, housing delicate ceiling frescoes and an ornate high altar.

Getting There

Located on the main transportation arteries of the Inn Valley, Hatting enjoys outstanding accessibility. By car, drivers take the Inntal Motorway A12 to the Zirl-West or Telfs-Ost exits, then continue along the provincial road L11 directly into Hatting. Rail passengers benefit from excellent train service: Hatting in Tirol railway station is served by Tyrol S-Bahn lines S4 and S5 every 30 minutes, connecting to Innsbruck Central Station in approximately 20 minutes. The renowned Inn Valley Cycle Path also runs directly past the town, allowing for scenic, eco-friendly arrivals on two wheels.

Tips

Culture seekers will appreciate a visit to the peaceful Parish Church of St. Giles in the village centre. For outdoor lovers and mountaineers, the Hattingerberg slopes serve as the launchpad for alpine adventures: A popular mountain trek ascends past the Archbrandhütte to the 2,308-metre summit of the Rauher Kopf, offering sweeping vistas of the Inn Valley and the Wetterstein range. Mountain bikers and e-bikers enjoy the scenic forest route up to the Inzinger Alm and onwards to the pristine Hundstalsee alpine lake, home to the stone Apollo Temple artwork. Down in the valley, the flat Inn Cycle Path is perfect for relaxing family rides.
